mainTopic: Is gold counted as money for redeeming מעשר שני and for loans? The גמרא looks at רבי יוחנן's view and at the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about swapping silver for gold.
overview: The גמרא starts with רבי יוחנן's rule that one may not borrow a gold dinar and repay a gold dinar. It first tries to prove from this that רבי יוחנן holds gold cannot redeem מעשר שני according to בית שמאי. It rejects that proof: loans are different, because in business the Rabbis treat gold like merchandise. רבין then reports that רבי יוחנן himself allowed redeeming with gold. Next comes another version, an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. One says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about swapping silver סלעים for gold דינרים, based on the idea of 'first money and not second money.' The other says they argue even about redeeming produce onto gold. Two משניות about changing a סלע are used to challenge the first opinion. רבא pushes off the case in ירושלים, but the case outside ירושלים forces the גמרא to agree that everyone allows 'second money.' The גמרא then begins restating the argument with a new reason, a protective rule of בית שמאי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No borrowing a dinar to repay a dinar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule of רבי יוחנן that a person may not borrow a dinar and pay it back with a dinar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden to borrow a dinar and repay it with a dinar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling of רבי יוחנן. It will use this ruling as a test case in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is רבית (interest). If the coin's value goes up before the loan is repaid, the lender gets back more than he lent. The גמרא now wants to work out which coin this rule is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of coin (silver or gold)
interest, which the Torah forbids on loans

phrases.english: It is forbidden to borrow a dinar for a dinar.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not lend a dinar on condition that it be repaid with a dinar, because of רבית.

steps.title: Which kind of dinar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of dinar the rule is talking about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: is this rule about a silver dinar or a gold dinar? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matters a great deal. Silver and gold have different legal status as money. Which coin is meant will show what רבי יוחנן thinks about gold.

phrases.english: A dinar of what?
phrases.notes: In other words, what metal is the coin made of?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dinar in רבי יוחנן's rule is silver or gold.

steps.title: It must be a gold dinar
steps.stepSummary: A silver dinar is surely money compared to silver, so the rule must be about a gold dinar.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a silver dinar repaid with a silver dinar, does anyone say that silver, compared to itself, is not money? So it is obvious that it means a gold dinar repaid with a gold dinar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out silver and concludes that the rule is talking about a gold dinar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver is the standard money. Paying back silver for silver is simply returning money, so there is no worry about רבית. A rule against it only makes sense if the coin is treated as merchandise that can rise in value, and that points to gold.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא דִּינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף בְּדִינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: If you say a silver dinar for a silver dinar,
relative to itself,
phrases.notes: Silver compared with silver, the same kind of coin.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָאו טִבְעָא הָוֵי?
phrases.english: is there anyone who says it is not currency?
Rather, it is obvious: a gold dinar
for a gold dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דִּינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף בְּדִינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule is about a gold dinar repaid with a gold dinar, since silver is certainly money relative to itself.

steps.title: Attempted proof: רבי יוחנן says gold cannot redeem מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The rule fits only בית שמאי, so it seems רבי יוחנן holds that for בית שמאי gold is not money, and one may not redeem מעשר שני with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is בית הלל, they say gold is currency. So it must be בית שמאי. Learn from this that רבי יוחנן is the one who said: we do not redeem with gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use this rule to settle an earlier question: which side did רבי יוחנן take about redeeming מעשר שני with gold according to בית שמאי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל treat gold as money, so for them a gold loan has no רבית worry. The rule must therefore follow בית שמאי. If רבי יוחנן treats gold as not-money in loans, it seems he would also say that gold cannot be used to redeem מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: we redeem (transfer the holiness of מעשר שני onto money)

phrases.english: And according to whom?
If according to בית הלל —
but they say it is currency.
Rather, is it not according to בית שמאי?
And learn from this that רבי יוחנן
is the one who said: we do not redeem!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier argument about whether, for בית שמאי, מעשר שני may be redeemed with gold dinars.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds that, according to בית שמאי, one does not redeem מעשר שני with gold dinars.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule forbidding borrowing a gold dinar for a gold dinar, which fits only בית שמאי's view that gold is not currency.

steps.title: Rejection: loans are a special case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן may still allow redeeming with gold. Loans are different, because in buying and selling the Rabbis treat gold like merchandise.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, רבי יוחנן says we do redeem with gold. But a loan is different: since the Rabbis treated gold like merchandise for buying and selling, saying that gold is what goes up and down in price, it is also merchandise when it comes to loans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The loan rule does not show what רבי יוחנן holds about מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if gold counts as money for redeeming מעשר שני, the Rabbis treat it as merchandise in business, because its price rises and falls. A loan is a business deal, so the same 'merchandise' treatment applies, and that creates the רבית worry. The proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: goes up and down in price

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא now says gold is never money. It says that only in buying, selling and loans the Rabbis treat gold like merchandise. For redeeming מעשר שני it can still count as money.

phrases.english: No, really, I will tell you,
רבי יוחנן is the one who said we do redeem.
But a loan is different,
since regarding buying and selling
the Rabbis made it like merchandise,
as we say: it is the one that goes up and down in price —
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's rule that in a gold-for-silver trade, gold is treated as the item being bought.

phrases.english: regarding a loan, too, it is merchandise.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the loan rule to the מעשר שני question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that gold's status in loans must match its status for redeeming מעשר שני. But loans follow the business rule that treats gold as merchandise.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one item can count as money for one law and as merchandise for another.

steps.title: Support from רבין: רבי יוחנן allows redeeming with gold
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן himself said: borrowing dinar for dinar is forbidden, yet one may redeem מעשר שני with a gold dinar. This supports the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, because when רבין came he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even though they said it is forbidden to borrow a dinar for a dinar, one may still redeem מעשר שני with it. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a direct quote from רבי יוחנן that backs up the answer it just gave, and the question is settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן himself puts the two rules side by side: gold loans are forbidden, but redeeming with gold is allowed. So he is the one who says 'we redeem,' just as the previous step suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: second tithe, which may be redeemed onto money

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that, for בית שמאי, one may redeem מעשר שני with a gold dinar. He still forbids borrowing a gold dinar for a gold dinar, because in business the Rabbis treat gold like merchandise.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
phrases.notes: רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל.

phrases.english: Even though they said
it is forbidden to borrow a dinar for a dinar,
still, we redeem מעשר שני with it.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds that one may redeem מעשר שני with a gold dinar, even though he forbids a gold loan repaid with gold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report of רבי יוחנן's statement putting both rules together.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן is the one who says 'מחללין': gold can redeem מעשר שני, while loans are a special case.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about changing a סלע
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that בית שמאי let מעשר שני money stay in copper coins. So surely they would allow gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone changes a סלע using copper coins of מעשר שני. בית שמאי say he may change the whole סלע into coins. בית הלל say half becomes a silver שקל and half stays in coins. Now, if בית שמאי let us redeem onto copper coins, do we even need to ask about gold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that, even according to בית שמאי, gold can be used for מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the מעשר שני money is in small copper coins, so בית שמאי accept that the produce was redeemed onto copper. Copper is a weaker kind of money than gold. So if copper works for בית שמאי, gold should work even more.

keyTerms.meaning: One who changes money from one kind of coin to another
We redeem, moving the holiness of מעשר שני onto money

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who changes a sela of second-tithe money,
phrases.notes: He has copper coins of מעשר שני money and is trading them for one silver סלע.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בְּכׇל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: for the whole sela, coins,
and Beit Hillel say:
one shekel in silver, one shekel kept in coins.
phrases.notes: A שקל is half a סלע, so בית הלל split it half and half.

phrases.english: Now, if according to Beit Shammai
we redeem onto copper coins,
is there any question about gold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that רבי יוחנן allows redeeming with gold, the גמרא looks for a source showing that even בית שמאי allow gold.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי allow redeeming מעשר שני with gold coins
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about changing a סלע of מעשר שני coins, where בית שמאי allow the whole amount in copper

steps.title: Copper coins are different because they spend easily
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: copper coins are special, because where people use them they are very easy to spend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Copper coins are different, because in a place where they are used, they move fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed copper is weaker money than gold, so gold should work too. The answer is that copper coins have a strength gold lacks: where they are used, everyone takes them easily. So allowing copper says nothing about gold.

keyTerms.meaning: Quick to spend, easy to use as money

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying copper is better money than gold everywhere. It only says that in a place where copper is used, it is easy to spend, and that is enough to break the proof.

phrases.english: Copper coins are different,
since in a place where they are used, they spend quickly.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide whether בית שמאי allow gold.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed copper is always weaker than gold, but copper spends easily where it is used, so it cannot teach us about gold.

steps.title: First opinion: the dispute is only about swapping silver for gold
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue. One says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about swapping silver סלעים for gold דינרים. Everyone agrees produce may be redeemed onto gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell it another way: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue. One says the dispute is about silver סלעים swapped for gold דינרים. בית שמאי learn from the פסוק 'the money' that it means the first money, not second money. בית הלל learn from 'the money' and 'money' that the extra word adds even second money. But redeeming produce onto gold דינרים is allowed by everyone, since that is still first money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the discussion, with an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and brings the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the only question is whether מעשר שני money may be swapped for new money. בית שמאי say only the money used to redeem the produce goes to ירושלים. בית הלל say the extra word in the פסוק allows swapping it for new money. Redeeming the produce itself onto gold is fine for everyone, because gold is then the first money.

keyTerms.meaning: Silver סלעים swapped for gold דינרים
First money: the coins the produce was first redeemed onto
Second money: new coins the first money was swapped for
The extra word adds something more

steps.whyThisMatters: By this opinion, nobody holds that gold cannot redeem produce. The whole dispute is only about swapping coins.

phrases.english: Some tell it in another version:
Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish argue.
One said: the dispute
is about silver selaim swapped for gold dinars,
for Beit Shammai hold:
"The money" means the first money
and not second money.
And Beit Hillel hold:
"The money", "money": the extra word adds,
even second money.
But produce redeemed onto dinars,
everyone agrees we redeem,
since it is still first money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a different version of the discussion, framed as an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about swapping silver for gold, since בית שמאי do not allow second money. Everyone agrees produce may be redeemed onto gold.

steps.title: Second opinion: they argue even about redeeming produce onto gold
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue even about redeeming produce onto gold דינרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: even about produce redeemed onto דינרים there is also a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second opinion in the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion makes the dispute wider. It is not only about swapping coins. It is about whether gold counts as money for redeeming at all, so בית שמאי would not allow redeeming produce onto gold.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views: (1) בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about swapping silver for gold, and everyone allows redeeming produce onto gold. (2) They argue even about redeeming produce onto gold.

phrases.english: And one said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּפֵירוֹת עַל דִּינָרִין נָמֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת.
phrases.english: even about produce redeemed onto dinars there is also a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to Step 9 in the same argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue even about redeeming produce onto gold דינרים.

steps.title: Why not argue about silver for silver?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about swapping silver סלעים for gold דינרים, the גמרא asks why they did not argue about the simpler case of silver for silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the argument is about silver סלעים for gold דינרים: instead of arguing about סלעים for דינרים, they should have argued about סלעים for סלעים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the opinion from Step 9. If swapping coins is the issue, why choose gold instead of the plain case of silver for silver?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever forbids silver for gold should surely also forbid silver for silver, because that is still swapping one coin for a second coin. So the clearer case seems to be silver for silver. The גמרא asks why the argument was not taught in that case.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says
the dispute is about silver סלעים for gold דינרים,
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from Step 9, which says everyone agrees produce may be redeemed onto gold.

phrases.english: instead of arguing about סלעים for דינרים,
let them argue about סלעים for סלעים!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר סְלָעִין עַל דִּינָרִין מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of the מחלוקת given in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the מחלוקת is only about silver סלעים for gold דינרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Silver for silver is the more basic case of swapping coins, so the argument should have been placed there.

steps.title: Gold was chosen to teach a new point
steps.stepSummary: Had they argued about silver for silver, we might think בית הלל agree that gold counts as a commodity next to silver. So the case of gold teaches that בית הלל allow even that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had argued about silver for silver, I would have said: that applies only to silver for silver. But with silver for gold, בית הלל would agree with בית שמאי that gold, compared to silver, is like merchandise, and we do not redeem onto it. So the case teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 11. The silver-for-gold case was chosen because it shows how far בית הלל go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compared to silver, gold is treated a bit like merchandise, and you cannot redeem money onto merchandise. If the argument were taught only about silver for silver, we would think בית הלל forbid gold. Teaching it with gold shows that בית הלל allow even this.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
Literally 'fruit'; here, a commodity or merchandise rather than real currency

steps.confusionAlert: פֵּירָא here does not mean actual fruit. It means gold acts like merchandise next to silver, not like currency.

phrases.english: If they had argued about סלעים for סלעים,
I would have said:
this applies only to סלעים for סלעים,
but with סלעים for דינרים,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדוּ לְהוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
phrases.english: בית הלל would agree with בית שמאי
that gold, compared to silver, is a commodity
and we do not redeem onto it,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִפְּלוּג בִּסְלָעִין עַל סְלָעִין, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: חידוש explanation: the harder case was chosen to show how far בית הלל's opinion goes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Had the case been silver for silver, we would think בית הלל forbid silver for gold, since gold is like merchandise next to silver.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל allow swapping silver even for gold.

steps.title: Proof from changing a סלע in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that in ירושלים one may change a silver סלע of מעשר שני into small coins. If silver can go to smaller coins, surely it can go to more valuable gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: one who changes a סלע of מעשר שני in ירושלים: בית שמאי say the whole סלע may be changed into small coins. בית הלל say: half into a silver שקל and half into small coins. Now, if we redeem silver onto small coins and do not say 'first money and not second money,' then onto gold, which is worth more, would we say 'first money and not second money'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge the opinion in Step 9, which says בית שמאי forbid switching מעשר שני silver onto gold because of 'first money and not second money'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, both sides let a silver סלע be changed into small copper coins, so they do not apply the rule 'first money and not second money.' The גמרא argues that switching to gold, which is even more valuable, should surely be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who changes a large coin into smaller ones
First money and not second money: the idea that מעשר שני money cannot be moved onto another set of money

phrases.english: Come hear:
one who changes a סלע of מעשר שני
in ירושלים,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בְּכׇל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת,
phrases.english: בית שמאי say: the whole סלע may be changed into small coins,
and בית הלל say:
a שקל's worth in silver and a שקל's worth in small coins.
phrases.notes: A סלע equals two שקלים, so בית הלל mean half stays silver and half becomes small coins.

phrases.english: Now, if we redeem silver onto small coins,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָמְרִינַן ״כֶּסֶף רִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא כֶּסֶף שֵׁנִי״,
phrases.english: and we do not say 'first money and not second money,'
then onto gold, which is worth more than it,

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן ״כֶּסֶף רִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא כֶּסֶף שֵׁנִי״?
phrases.english: would we say 'first money and not second money'?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of Step 9, which bases בית שמאי's ruling on 'first money and not second money'.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני money may be switched onto gold coins
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מעשר שני about changing a סלע in ירושלים

steps.title: רבא: ירושלים is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. In ירושלים the Torah allows spending the money on anything, so changing coins there tells us nothing about outside ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: you are bringing a challenge from ירושלים? ירושלים is different, because about it the Torah writes: 'And you shall spend the money on whatever your soul desires, on cattle or on sheep.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge of Step 13: the משנה deals only with ירושלים, so it cannot disprove the opinion of Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים the מעשר שני money is meant to be spent freely, so breaking a coin into change for spending is natural there. That does not show that one may switch the money onto gold outside ירושלים. The rule 'first money and not second money' can still apply outside.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about changing coins in ירושלים cannot decide the question of switching to gold, because ירושלים has a special פסוק letting the money be spent on anything.

phrases.english: רבא said:
You are bringing a challenge from ירושלים?
ירושלים is different,
because it is written about it:
'And you shall spend the money on whatever your soul desires,'
'on cattle or on sheep.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with ירושלים, where a פסוק allows the money to be spent freely, so it cannot teach the rule outside ירושלים.

steps.title: Even בית שמאי allow changing coins
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that בית שמאי let a person change copper מעשר שני coins into a silver סלע. So they clearly allow moving מעשר שני money onto other coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone changes copper coins of מעשר שני money for a silver סלע. בית שמאי say he may trade coins for the whole סלע. בית הלל say he may trade for a silver שקל (half), and the other שקל's worth stays in copper coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to attack the earlier explanation of בית שמאי's view. In this משנה, בית שמאי openly allow switching coins onto other coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation assumed בית שמאי do not allow מעשר שני money to move onto a second set of coins. But here, even outside ירושלים, בית שמאי allow trading copper מעשר שני coins for a whole silver סלע, which is exactly that kind of exchange. So that explanation of בית שמאי cannot be right.
steps.confusionAlert: Here בית שמאי are the more lenient side: they allow changing the whole סלע's worth. בית הלל allow only half. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who changes a סלע
from coins of מעשר שני –
phrases.notes: This time the case is outside ירושלים: he trades copper coins of מעשר שני for one silver סלע.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בְּכׇל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת,
phrases.english: בית שמאי say: for the whole סלע, coins,
and בית הלל say:
for a שקל, silver; for a שקל, coins!
phrases.notes: A שקל is half a סלע: half the copper is traded for silver, and half stays in copper coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע מִמְּעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from ירושלים was rejected, the גמרא brings a new משנה that challenges the earlier explanation of בית שמאי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation that בית שמאי forbid moving מעשר שני money onto a second set of coins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי openly allow trading copper מעשר שני coins for a silver סלע outside ירושלים, which is a coin-to-coin exchange.

steps.title: Everyone agrees even second money is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier explanation. Everyone agrees that the extra word הכסף in the פסוק comes to include even 'second money'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees: the Torah's extra word 'the money' adds more, and includes even second money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and changes its explanation. Now both sides agree that מעשר שני money may be moved onto other coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra mention of הכסף in the פסוק teaches that even coins which already replaced earlier coins ('second money') can hold מעשר שני. So the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל cannot be about whether a coin-to-coin exchange is allowed at all. A new reason for their argument is needed, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Second money': coins that took the place of earlier מעשר שני coins

steps.whyThisMatters: This clears the way for a new explanation of the argument. It is about which kinds of coins may be used, not about whether exchanging coins is allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
'the money': the word 'money' includes more,
phrases.notes: דברים 14:25–26. The פסוק says הכסף again, and that extra word comes to teach something more.

phrases.english: even second money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from step 15 and replaces the earlier reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the earlier explanation is dropped and a new shared reading of the פסוק is given
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought בית שמאי forbid putting מעשר שני onto second coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone learns from the extra word הכסף that even second money is allowed.

steps.title: Rewording the argument of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש. One of them says the argument is about silver סלעים onto gold דינרים, because בית שמאי make a protective rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש was said, this is how it was said: One said the argument is about changing silver סלעים into gold דינרים, because בית שמאי hold that we make a protective rule...
steps.whatsHappening: Since the old explanation fell, the גמרא restates the two אמוראים' argument in a new form. This line starts the new version, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight is no longer about whether coins can be exchanged at all, since everyone allows that. The first opinion says בית שמאי forbid silver-to-gold only because of a גזירה, a protective rule made by the Rabbis. The details of the גזירה come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said (introduces a new version of a dispute)

steps.confusionAlert: Here בית שמאי's reason is a Rabbinic protective rule, not a reading of the פסוק. The פסוק itself, as everyone now agrees, allows coin exchanges.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: the argument of רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש,
this is how it was said:
One said: the argument is
about silver סלעים onto gold דינרים,
since בית שמאי hold: we make a protective rule
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where we find out what the rule is meant to prevent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, הָכִי אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 16. Since everyone allows coin exchanges, the אמוראים' argument is restated with a new reason for בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא holds the argument is about silver סלעים onto gold דינרים, and בית שמאי forbid it because of a protective rule.
